full_judgment: "It think this is to be presumed. But the foundation for the presumption, in the case of a person under detention or on licence, is the legality of the detention, and the necessity for a licence to justify the patient's absence, and if it is shown and admitted, as in the present case, that, on the face of the documents produced and received in evidence without objection, the detention was illegal, the whole basis of the sub -section and the presumption of defectiveness goes and the prosecution must fail". '"
